note: THE SHAPE s-word-wrap PRODUCES: a temp buffer, a let-bound `fill-column', fill the whole buffer, read it back. Emacs answers ("" "aa bb\ncc dd" 12) and all three elements are contract. The RETURN VALUE is the fill prefix that was used -- the empty string here, `"  "' in frontier-fill-region-adaptive-prefix -- and not nil and not the buffer text. POINT ENDS AT POINT-MAX rather than where it started, so a caller that cares has to save its own excursion; s-word-wrap does not care, because it reads the whole buffer afterwards. kg answers `void-function' at this pin.
